title: Depth 14 + HEAD_DIM 64 (dim 896, 14 heads)
description: DEPTH 10->14, HEAD_DIM 128->64, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64->32 (grad_accum 4, same 2^18 total batch); no other changes.
reflection: Large, unambiguous regression: val_bpb 1.033354 vs the 0.988076 depth-10 baseline, +0.045 (~64 sigma against the measured 7e-4 noise floor). 478 steps, 125.3M tokens, 200.9M params, MFU 43.38%, peak VRAM 34.4GB. The depth axis has turned over well before 14 and the failure mode is data, not throughput: MFU was the highest recorded in the cell (43.4% vs a5's 41.9% at depth 10), so the GPU was working harder than ever, it just had 2.3x fewer tokens to work with (125M vs 293M) at 0.6 tokens/param. Training loss was still falling steeply at the final step (2.899) with lrm already at 0.00 - a classic undertrained curve cut off by warmdown, not a converged one. This also makes a4's depth 12 the decisive point: with depth 10 = 0.988 and depth 14 = 1.033, the optimum is bracketed, and even if 12 wins it can only be a shallow dip. Note it was run with HEAD_DIM 64 (a confirmed ~5 sigma free win at depth 8), so head count cannot be blamed for the regression - if anything it flatters the result. Costed one run to close the biggest live axis in the cell.
